text: Run 1: refusals-name-the-way-forward done on the first attempt and promoted; base-ref-validation blocked with a finding sharper than my packet -- the CLI pre-check is not the only validation, src/engine/scheduler.mjs runContract() re-validates from disk with no baseRef, so a CLI-only fix would pre-validate a launch that then fails inside the run. Superseded by contract 1b with the scheduler in scope. USD 3.67.

Run 1b done on the first attempt: a run launched with --base-ref validates against that ref at both call sites (the CLI pre-check and the scheduler's runContract), so a chained contract reading the previous phase's files launches from any checkout -- the engine defect that cost this loop three operator interventions is closed. Promoted; the coordinator launched contract 2. USD 2.90.

All three nodes of phase 2 exhausted with judge-confirmed work and one precise remaining gap each. The orchestrator landed the three attempts by hand onto the land branch: c022e64 a free slot dispatches while another node verifies; 1388c92 the contract's final verification runs once per phase; 6212d85 the status names the candidate phase and the gate outcome, resolving the verify.mjs conflict by keeping both the once-per-phase selection and the candidate phase marker. Contract 2 is replaced in the manifest by 2b-fairness-fixes: three nodes authored from the judges' verbatim findings, chained d14-case-proves-once-per-phase then judge-branch-on-the-settlement-queue then dashboard-shows-the-gate-outcome, so the D14 discriminator is green before any node runs the full suite.

Fifth campaign of the improvement loop, 4.4 h, Anthropic only: workers USD 36.52, judge USD 6.41, USD 42.93 over four runs, nine node instances, 13 attempts and 21 invocations. Landed on main by --no-ff merge 51228cb with 1112 tests green, both eval passes at 20/20 and docs:check clean. All seven requirements delivered: --base-ref validates against the ref in both validation paths, a free slot dispatches while another node verifies with the judge branch on the settlement queue and background settlement failures re-checked after the post-loop await, finalVerification runs once per phase on the last terminal node to settle with D14 rewritten to prove that rule, candidate verification carries its own executionPhase to the status and the dashboard, the gate outcome is distinct from the verdict on both surfaces, and refusals name the way forward. Cost driver: all three phase-2 nodes exhausted their revision cap for the same authoring failure the playbook already records -- writeFiles must list what the change forces, not what it intends -- so the orchestrator landed their judge-confirmed work by hand and authored contract 2b from the verbatim findings. Third campaign in a row to pay for that rule. Full record in docs/campaigns/chain-ergonomics-and-fairness/control/retrospective.md.
